body:
Review finding on #757 (read-only pass), the same wrong-form class that PR retires, but with membership consequences.

`Nah2po4_X_2_H2o.yaml` (local identity `kgmicrobe.compound:nah2po4_x_2_h2o`, the dihydrate label) carries six `HYDRATE_FORM` synonyms from kg-microbe, three of which are **monohydrate** spellings: `NaH2PO4 x H2O`, `NaH2PO4·H2O`, `NaH2PO4・H2O`. The monohydrate has its own record, `Sodium_phosphate_monobasic_monohydrate` (CHEBI:114249), which after #755 also owns the raw `NaH2PO4•H2O` labels.

CultureMech's occurrence table names those three strings in **36 recipes** (34 + 1 + 1) and resolves all of them to `CHEBI:37585`, the anhydrous `NaH2PO4`, so the anhydrous record's membership and counts include 36 monohydrate recipes; the dihydrate spellings (`x 2H2O`, `·2H2O`, `・2H2O`, 4 recipes) resolve there too.

Fix, in the batch-3/4 shape: move the three monohydrate strings onto the monohydrate record (`REJECTED_LABEL` on the dihydrate), add `SOURCE_LABEL_IDENTIFIER_OVERRIDES` entries for all six spellings (three → CHEBI:114249, three → the dihydrate local id), move the membership edges off CHEBI:37585, and refresh the three records' counts from the edges. Fixed in #757's review round.

Related: #232, #459, #755.

comments.body:
Implemented as `scripts/move_nah2po4_hydrate_labels.py` on the #757 branch and verified locally (3 spellings moved, 40 memberships moved: NaH2PO4 237 → 197, dihydrate 53 → 57, monohydrate 50 → 86; all gates green) — then reverted from that PR, because the count refresh on `Nah2po4.yaml` hits the same pin as #740:

```
ValueError: Identity plan no longer describes current record: data/ingredients/mapped/Nah2po4.yaml
```

`reports/semantic_review_20260921/corrections/identity-plan.json` pins the anhydrous record byte-for-byte (its "Sodium dihydrogen phosphate" identity correction from 2026-09-21), and `build_review.py` refuses any later edit. Leaving the memberships under CHEBI:37585 while moving the strings would make `test_the_counts_are_reproducible_from_the_edges` fail on the next membership rebuild, so the whole move waits together. The script stays in the repo with the blocker documented; it and the six `SOURCE_LABEL_IDENTIFIER_OVERRIDES` entries it requires run as one step once #740 makes identity-plan records supersedable.

Observed during the full current-owner Step 7d review for #901 at main `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`. These are proposed corrections or explicit deferrals before source writes; structural validation is not scientific approval. Exact owner preimages, primary-source capture hashes and full rubrics are prepared under `reports/step7d_mapping_901_20261103/` for the implementation PR.

`Nah2po4_X_2_H2o` is dropped in full from Step 7d. The exact dihydrate candidate [NCIT:C66551](https://api-evsrest.nci.nih.gov/api/v1/concept/ncit/C66551?include=full) and CAS 13472-35-0 are now locally resolved and source-compatible candidates, but that discovery does not settle the coupled owner/alias/membership correction already documented here.

The current dihydrate record still carries the three monohydrate strings `NaH2PO4 x H2O`, `NaH2PO4·H2O`, and `NaH2PO4・H2O` as `HYDRATE_FORM`. The prior comment explains why moving the labels without the six source-label overrides and membership/count changes would leave inconsistent ownership, and why the attempted repair was reverted after the #740 identity-plan pin failed. Those historical 36/40-occurrence numbers are not asserted as a new recount.

Recommendation: keep this owner and all memberships/counts unchanged in Step 7d, retain this issue’s full three-owner scope, and evaluate the exact dihydrate promotion in the same bounded follow-up as the monohydrate alias transfer, all six source-label overrides and membership-derived counts. Reassess the current #740/native receipt route at implementation time; do not assume that the historical workaround or stale pin is still the exact current mechanism.

Acceptance remains coupled: distinguish anhydrous, mono- and dihydrate identities from primary evidence; preserve the original labels as rejected provenance on the wrong-form owner; direct recipe memberships to the evidenced owner; recompute all affected counts; synchronize the native mapping and companion receipt without carrying inherited support onto changed owner bytes. No isolated alias-only fix, automatic exact-term promotion, role approval or owner merge is part of Step 7d. #758 remains open.

title: NaH2PO4 monohydrate spellings sit on the dihydrate record and their 36 recipe occurrences count toward anhydrous NaH2PO4
